results.title: Matīss Kaža. The Impossible Self-Portrait
results.overview: The film follows Matīss Kaža during a period when his professional life has taken him from one country and continent to another. Together with Gints Zilbalodis, the director of the film Flow (Straume), he spent nearly a year caught in a whirlwind of international award ceremonies, events, and meetings—a journey that included the film’s path to the Academy Awards. Yet, this is only one facet of Kaža’s life and work. During the same period, he made his debut as a theatre director at three different venues in Riga and crafted the Lielais Kristaps (Latvian National Film Awards) and Spēlmaņu nakts (Latvian Theatre Awards) ceremonies as multimedia performances. The camera follows Kaža as he constantly creates, travels, and engages in new projects, all while maintaining an ironic perspective on both himself and the world around him.

results.title: HOME TV
results.overview: A host for HOME TV finds herself in the heart of life on Kyiv’s central streets. Asking locals, displaced people, and visitors of the capital “what is home?”, she comes across different views and circumstances. The collage of answers gradually blurs the question itself, leaving her face-to-face with her own search.

results.title: Selma
results.overview: Neslihan, an unsuccessful actress, and her social media influencer friends break into the home of Selma—a woman suffering from Alzheimer’s—to secretly live-stream her for profit. As their viewership surges, the house begins to reveal its terrifying secrets, and the young women find themselves trapped in a lethal Dark Web show. Now, Neslihan must decide just how far she is willing to go to escape poverty and achieve fame.

results.title: The Last Act: Ediz Hun
results.overview: A biographical documentary that chronicles Ediz Hun’s 83-year journey—spanning cinema, academia, and theater—through his roles as an actor, ecologist, and collector, as well as his insatiable curiosity.

results.overview: Across Arunachal Pradesh, women carry generations of ancestral forest knowledge. Gathering plants, herbs and other produce, they sustain their families while preserving a deep relationship with the forest amid growing social, economic and environmental pressures.

results.title: Still Life
results.overview: On a split screen two parallel and contrasting narratives unfold. The world of art and the realm of the everyday are integrally connected and yet hugely disparate. A pair of hands working relentlessly inside a home fade away; while a painting hanging quietly in a museum gains fame.
